```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
root <- "C:/Users/kwizerah/Desktop/AUCA/R-programming/ASSIGNMENT 1"
data_dir <- file.path(root, "data")
```

## Goal

Practice the data-importation part of [Class_R for data science](https://rpubs.com/Mapara_lee/1434996):

1. Install helpful packages  
2. Import data from different sources  
3. Show how each library helps explore those datasets  

## Packages and what they are for

| Source | Package | Main function |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| Text / CSV | `readr` / base R | `read_csv()`, `read.table()` |
| Excel | `readxl` | `read_excel()` |
| SPSS / Stata / SAS | `haven` | `read_sav()`, `read_dta()`, `read_sas()` |
| Database (SQLite) | `DBI` + `RSQLite` | `dbConnect()`, `dbReadTable()`, `dbGetQuery()` |

```{r packages}
# install.packages(c("readr","readxl","haven","DBI","RSQLite","writexl"))
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(haven)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
```

## 1. Text file (lecturer style)

```{r text}
data_class <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "class_data.txt"), header = TRUE)
variable.names(data_class)
head(data_class)
summary(data_class)
str(data_class)
```

## 2. Excel (`readxl`)

```{r excel}
excel_path <- file.path(data_dir, "class_workbook.xlsx")
excel_sheets(excel_path)
excel_students <- read_excel(excel_path, sheet = "students")
summary(excel_students)
```

`readxl` reads `.xlsx` without needing Excel installed, and can pick a sheet by name.

## 3. SPSS and Stata — HW1 statistical packages (`haven`)

```{r spss-stata}
students_spss <- read_sav(file.path(data_dir, "students.sav"))
students_stata <- read_dta(file.path(data_dir, "students.dta"))
head(students_spss)
summary(as.data.frame(students_spss))
head(students_stata)
```

`haven` imports SPSS/Stata/SAS files and keeps labelled data (variable/value labels) that plain CSV drops.

## 4. Database — HW1 DBMS (`DBI` + `RSQLite`)

```{r database}
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), file.path(data_dir, "class_db.sqlite"))
dbListTables(con)
db_class <- dbReadTable(con, "class_data")
female_students <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM students WHERE gender = 'F'")
sql_summary <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT gender,
         COUNT(*) AS n,
         ROUND(AVG(math_score), 2) AS mean_math,
         ROUND(AVG(it_score), 2) AS mean_it
  FROM students
  GROUP BY gender
")
dbDisconnect(con)

head(db_class)
female_students
sql_summary
```

`DBI` gives one API for many databases; `RSQLite` lets you practice SQL locally. You can filter and aggregate **before** loading everything into R.

## 5. Quick exploration (from class notes)

```{r explore}
BMI <- round(data_class$WEIGHT / (data_class$HEIGHT / 100)^2, 2)
summary(BMI)
plot(WEIGHT ~ HEIGHT, data = data_class, main = "WEIGHT vs HEIGHT")
abline(lm(WEIGHT ~ HEIGHT, data = data_class)$coefficients)
cor(data_class$HEIGHT, data_class$WEIGHT)
```

## How the libraries help (short answers)

- **`readr` / `read.table`**: bring plain text/CSV into a data frame for `summary()`, plots, and models.  
- **`readxl`**: pull spreadsheet sheets without manual copy-paste.  
- **`haven`**: reuse SPSS/Stata/SAS project files; labels survive the import.  
- **`DBI` + `RSQLite`**: query large tables with SQL, then analyze the result in R.
